notes.tech: Thread proposed 2 (2026-10-11): OrthoLite Hybrid insole (licensed); Vibram leather outsole (1 style); apple leather upper on Vegan 01 (4 colourways); house-named Casetta rubber sole (50% natural, 40% recycled, 10% conventional); LWG-certified leather (a certification, not tech) — licensed (OrthoLite, Vibram); Casetta sole is a house name; share of range OrthoLite named on 93 of 100 footwear products in /products.json; Vibram 1 of 10. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.
notes.craft: Thread proposed 2 (2026-10-11): Koio states the country on every shoe and the city (Florence or Porto) on most, and describes its Florence partner (family-run, all steps under one roof, 42 craftspeople per pair), but names no maker and owns nothing. A named tannery appears only on one collaboration style. That is a well-stated country with process claims, short of the named makers or mills a 3 needs. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.

craft_evidence.owned: no: brand says it partners with an unnamed manufacturer in Florence ("third-generation family business", all steps under one roof); claim only, no named place or photograph of ownership
craft_evidence.makers: no: factory unnamed on PDPs and pages; Italian-craftsmanship page names only "Gianluca, our head lastmaker" of an unnamed last-making firm (70 years)
craft_evidence.mills: 1 of 100 footwear products: Capri Rose Anvil (a collaboration) names Conceria Brotini (Pisa) and Conceria Carpanese (Vicenza); all other PDPs say only Italian calf leather / LWG-certified
craft_evidence.madein: 100 of 100 footwear products in the feed state a country in body copy (Italy/Tuscany/Florence 79; Porto/Portugal 21); FAQ: Ostuni line Spain, Pale Blue Dot and Carrara Portugal
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed but young: founded 2014 in New York City by Johannes Quodt and Chris Wichert (FAQ)
craft_evidence.process: partly: about page says 34 factories visited, every pair passes through 42 craftspeople, cutting to boxing under one roof; soles, leather and boxes sourced near Florence; no construction method documented beyond that
craft_evidence.reasoning: Koio states the country on every shoe and the city (Florence or Porto) on most, and describes its Florence partner (family-run, all steps under one roof, 42 craftspeople per pair), but names no maker and owns nothing. A named tannery appears only on one collaboration style. That is a well-stated country with process claims, short of the named makers or mills a 3 needs.
